source.title: Reading Between the Dots: Decoding Hidden Computation across Filler Tokens
source.authors: K. Brauer; C. M. Verdun; Samuel Marks

page_placements.theme: Answers or decisions formed latently, before or apart from the visible chain of thought

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether filler-position representations contain task intermediates and causally affect later answers, using logit-lens measurements and KV-cache transplants rather than the original rhyme-planning setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports behavioral accuracy, residual-stream readouts, attention measurements, and causal KV-cache transplant outcomes. It also describes several decoding controls and supplemental breakdowns; the rows below record the principal results bearing on the claim, not every per-condition decoding-table entry. The study does not test rhyming verse.
record.test_reason: The study bears on V3 in a new setting: filler tokens inserted between question and answer. At filler positions the next token is always a dot, yet intermediate values (A1, A2, y) are decodable there. KV-cache transplants confined to filler positions shift the later answer. So features computed at earlier positions are used at later ones. It does not test rhyme planning (V1, V4) or future-token prediction (V2): the decoded quantities are task intermediates, not upcoming tokens. It does not test plan-like look-ahead (V5, V6). Behavioral accuracy uplift does not measure look-ahead.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that, on cleanly decomposable non-adversarial tasks, filler positions carry intermediate computation that causally feeds the answer and can be decoded without supervision. Interpretability monitoring can thus partly close the CoT-monitorability gap. They add that filler computation resembles ordinary single-pass computation spread across positions, not written step-by-step reasoning.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses inserted filler tokens, logit-lens residual readouts, attention analysis, and KV-cache transplants on arithmetic, lookup, and equation tasks; it does not use a rhyme-generation intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Filler type and length affect behavioral uplift; scrambled filler underperforms, very long filler can asymptote or degrade, and filler before the question gives no uplift. Residual subtraction helps in some settings and hurts in others; judge prompts and task framing change decoding results.

fits_no_version.finding: Content-free filler tokens between question and answer raise no-CoT accuracy across tasks and models. The gain is absent for Qwen 3 480B on addition, and filler placed before the question gives no gain.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models perform extra latent computation over filler tokens, improving no-CoT multi-step accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: With filler present, attention from the answer position shifts from the question to the filler region (question 15.8% to 3-4%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Filler tokens form a question → filler → answer attention relay.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026), as stated in the paper
record.problems: The study covers two instruction-tuned models in depth and one reasoning-trained model on one task. Tasks are deliberately cleanly decomposable and non-adversarial. Most mechanistic and decoding analyses use 4-bit checkpoints, although selected analyses are checked on native FP8. The filler-versus-CoT comparison is described as a visual aggregate on one task. Causal transplants sometimes change or corrupt the target answer rather than fully swapping it.
record.rows_left_out: Not stated; no rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No rhyming verse, rhyme-word representation or intervention.
Decodes task intermediates, not tokens several positions ahead; the sum appears only at the answer position.
Does not test whether the filler computation arises because training rewards later use, versus a side effect. Only inserted-filler settings with cleanly decomposable tasks are tested.
No rhyme planning in open models.
No measure of look-ahead to future outputs or plans; accuracy uplift only. No chess or Sokoban.
No test of plan horizon or of plans steering generation.

missing.what: Kimi K2.5 (reasoning-trained) direct decoding: both addends in top-2 in 80.6% of correct 2-fact examples at filler positions.
Per-intermediate decoding on system of equations. The given input x is barely present (top-5 21.9%), while computed y is 94.8% and c2y 85.6%. The filler encodes computed values, not copied input.
On incorrect 2-fact examples the sum is essentially absent at filler positions while the addends remain (top-2 sum 21.7% vs 2.0%, DeepSeek V3).
Filler-vs-CoT layout: under filler, chain intermediates spread across positions in the same depth order as single-pass computation. This is a visual aggregate only.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. It is framed around CoT monitorability, not planning; the link to V3 is that filler positions predict only a dot yet hold intermediates used later. Most mechanistic results use 4-bit checkpoints; the DeepSeek 2-fact analysis was checked on FP8. Transplants were run only on DeepSeek V3.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse task, candidate rhyme-word representation, or rhyme-word intervention.
Tests single-state readout of selected numeric intermediates in one task/model setting quantitatively; does not test arbitrary future-token prediction or a broad range of distances.

Does not isolate whether the computation was formed specifically for later positions rather than as a consequence of local next-token prediction; tasks use inserted filler positions and cleanly decomposable problems.
Open-weight models are studied, but not rhyme planning or open attribution-graph tools.
Tests arithmetic, letter-position, and in-context equation tasks in language models; does not test chess, Sokoban, or other architectures.

Causal transplants test whether filler-position content matters, but do not establish that the mechanism is not also shaped by local next-token features or heuristics; no explicit look-ahead-distance sweep.

statements.correction: System of equations: direct top-2 recovery 82.1% (Section 6.4); direct top-5 recovery 94.8%, shuffled direct top-5 recovery 1.3% (Table 9). statements.problem: The 82.1% recovery and 1.3% shuffled control use different K values. Several other decoding values follow the main text but conflict with Figure 6 and appendix tables.
The cited decoding rates match Section 6.2 but are internally inconsistent with Table 3/Figure 6; weaker decoding does not establish absence of the underlying computation.

statements.correction: Kimi K2.5: reasoning-trained; explicit reasoning suppressed with an empty think block; both addends recovered in direct top-2 tokens in 80.6% of correct examples, n = 962, dots-10/25 pooled (Section 6.2; Appendix O; Table 17). Explicit reasoning enabled: untested.
statements.problem: Reasoning-trained models are not wholly untested: Kimi K2.5 has a direct intermediate-decoding result, as well as the behavioral results already present in r12 and r13.

statements.correction: Measurements: filler-position intermediate decoding and causal later use through KV-cache transplants. No training-incentive manipulation or myopic-training comparison reported.
